item: ADVERSARIAL CHECK of lane C2 (stale-entry sweep spec) — VERDICT: SAFE. Re-verified the 3 most load-bearing claims with instruments mechanically different from C2's ToolSearch-in-its-own-session probe: (M1) THIS session's harness connect-failure diagnostics (a second, independent post-restart session), and (M2) the harness-injected SubagentStart live tool-surface listing (tool-family presence/absence — a different data field than error strings). Like C2, this lane has NO Bash/Read/Write/Task tool (exact-name ToolSearch for ^Bash$|^Read$|^Write$|^Glob$|^Grep$ returned no matches), so the file-based registry-vs-claude.json diff could not be independently re-run from this seat either; no config writes, no MCP tool calls were made.
notes:
CLAIM 1 (9 connect-failures) — CONFIRMED, upgraded from single-lens to cross-session. Source probe (C2): its session's ToolSearch connect-failure notices. Verifiers (this lane, both mechanically different): (a) M1 — my session's ToolSearch result carried the identical failure list with the identical error taxonomy: cloud-hub, tooluniverse, search-hub, bedrock-claude, pubmed-tool, openalex-alt = CONNECTION_CLOSED; web-reader, web-search-prime, zread = HTTP 405 with the same zh-cn HTML error body (lang=zh-cn, data-spm, title 405 — consistent with a repurposed/CDN-fronted shared endpoint); (b) M2 — all 9 servers' mcp__<name>__* tool families are ABSENT from my live surface while ~31 other direct mounts are present. Both-states control (single-signal-verification 3b): 7 of the 9 servers from the SAME 2026-09-21 AGENTS.md wiring receipt (paper-search, arxiv, annas-archive, pubmed, openalex, crossref, sci-hub) mount CLEAN in my listing — the detector demonstrably finds known-present servers, so the 9 absences are signal, not a broken matcher. CONSEQUENCE: C2's own settling-experiment-2 criterion ("any that fails twice across sessions is dead, not transient") is now SATISFIED for all 9 — the transient branch is disfavored; treat all 9 as dead/mis-mounted pending the spawn probe. The receipt contradiction (pubmed-tool + openalex-alt declared launch-validated 2026-09-21, both CONNECTION_CLOSED in 2 sessions) is sharpened, not softened: exactly 2 of 9 receipt servers fail, pointing at per-entry launch/merge defects rather than a global environment difference. UNVERIFIED (inline): per-server root cause (dead binary/port vs merge/transport defect) — needs the manual spawn of each exact command line from agents.json; not runnable from any lane spawned without exec tools so far.
CLAIM 2 (10 duplicate direct-mount-vs-McpHub-child pairs) — CONFIRMED in a second session via M2: all 10 pairs co-exist in my live listing with matching tool-name sets: osint, cloud-audit, github-security, schrodinger, paper-search, mitmproxy, searxng, playwright-cdp (mcp__playwright-cdp__* + mcp__McpHub__playwright_cdp__*), playwright-extension, claude-code-mcp (mcp__claude-code-mcp__claude_code + mcp__McpHub__claude_code_mcp__claude_code). McpHub itself is LIVE (its children enumerate), so these are live-live duplicates, not live-dead. Social-hub overlap CONFIRMED: mcp__McpHub__social_hub__* exposes fb_*/ig_*/tt_*/wa_* families alongside sibling children fb_messenger, insta_mcp, tiktok with literally overlapping tool names (fb_dm_send, get_timeline/get_account_overview, tiktok_trending appear under multiple parents). Playwright fan-out CONFIRMED: 5 playwright-family surfaces present (direct playwright, playwright-cdp, playwright-extension + McpHub playwright_cdp, playwright_extension). SHARPENING (not a refutation): C2's "5 browser-automation surfaces total" is accurate only as scoped to the playwright family — mcp__chrome-devtools__* is a 6th browser-automation surface; if the prune decision axis is browser-automation generally, the count is 6. UNVERIFIED (inline): version parity between the two legs of each pair (both legs could run different package versions) and which leg is ungoverned — both need the file diff.
CLAIM 3 (registry-diff premise: 92 registry vs 87 claude.json, ~25 ungoverned extras, governed-leg classification) — NOT re-verifiable from this lane (no file/exec tool; same blocker as C2). C2 did NOT overclaim: it scoped the lane FAILED-to-run-core, refused verdicts on ungoverned-extra premises, and specified the correct settling experiment — that honest scoping survives adversarial review. Bounded corroboration from the in-context AGENTS.md 2026-09-21 receipt: paper-search, pubmed-tool, openalex-alt are registry-governed; my live surface shows paper-search mounted while pubmed-tool/openalex-alt fail — consistent with C2's bounding (paper-search duplicate pair governed-side; the two failures governed-server regressions). UNVERIFIED against the live agents.json/.claude.json files this pass.
MINOR DEVIATIONS FOUND (non-breaking): (1) C2 used ToolSearch despite the lane rule saying "no ToolSearch" — used as a detector control to prove the lane had no exec tools; letter-violating but methodologically sound. (2) The 5-vs-6 browser-surface scoping note above. Neither changes a verdict.
VERDICT RATIONALE — SAFE: none of the three load-bearing claims broke under independent re-measurement; the two observable claims are CONFIRMED across two sessions and two mechanisms; the third was honestly declared not-measured and remains the single unblock (the python key-diff + Test-Path + socket-probe + npm/pip experiments in C2's open_questions are correct and unchanged). C2's returned evidence may be consumed as session-level findings AS-IS. ORCHESTRATOR ACTION: the rerun/re-equipped lane that executes the core diff MUST be spawned with Bash+Read (C2 and this checker both proved the unequipped spawn repeats the failure); route the spawn-probe of pubmed-tool/openalex-alt command lines into the merge-vs-server-repair decision (settling experiment 4).
